questions.q: What whisper went around the forecastle one night at about eleven o'clock?
choices: That Shuan had done for him at last
That the ship had struck a rock
That the captain had fallen overboard
That land had been sighted to the west
questions.evidence: Shuan had done for him at last

questions.q: Why did the captain come down and send David to the round-house?
choices: David was to be punished for stealing food
David was needed to help steer in the storm
David and Ransome were to change berths
David was to be locked away from the crew
questions.evidence: You and Ransome are to change berths

questions.q: Why was the sunset still bright so late at night?
choices: The brig was already more than half-way across the Atlantic
The light came from a lighthouse on the Isle of May
The brig was going north round Scotland, near Orkney and Shetland
A great fire was burning on a ship near the brig
questions.evidence: we were going north-about round Scotland

questions.q: What was kept in the round-house besides the officers' berths?
choices: The sails, ropes and tools for mending the ship
The best food and drink, the powder and the firearms
The ship's cargo of tobacco leaf and bales of cloth
The sailors' sea-chests and their spare clothes
questions.evidence: all the best of the meat and drink and the whole of the powder

questions.q: What did Mr. Riach do with Mr. Shuan's brandy bottle?
choices: Drank it all himself
Tossed it into the sea
Locked it in a locker
Gave it to the captain
questions.evidence: he tossed the bottle into the sea

questions.q: What excuse did Mr. Shuan give for what he had done to Ransome?
choices: He brought me a dirty pannikin
He was rude to the captain
He stole a bottle of brandy
He would not stop his loud singing
questions.evidence: he brought me a dirty pannikin!

questions.q: What story did the captain say must be told in Dysart about Ransome?
choices: That the boy died of a fever
That the boy ran away at a port
That the boy went overboard
That the boy was lost in a storm
questions.evidence: The boy went overboard, sir; that's what the story is

questions.q: Why does David think Mr. Riach and the captain were so patient with him in the round-house?
choices: They had learned that he was really the heir of Shaws
They were hoping to sell him for a higher price as a servant
They felt guilty about how badly Ransome had been treated
They were afraid that he would tell the crew about Shuan
questions.evidence: they would scarce have been so good with me if they had not been worse with Ransome

questions.q: How did Mr. Shuan behave toward David after Ransome's death?
choices: He beat him every day, just as he had once beaten Ransome
He was very kind and gave him money and good food
He stared at him, sometimes with terror, and drew back from him
He never looked at him and would not speak to him
questions.evidence: stared at me continually (sometimes, I could have thought, with terror)

questions.q: How did the one survivor of the boat that the brig ran down save himself?
choices: He swam to the brig and climbed up a rope ladder
He clung to a piece of the broken boat until the dawn
He leaped up and caught hold of the brig's bowsprit
He was pulled from the water by Mr. Riach's crew
questions.evidence: had leaped up and caught hold of the brig's bowsprit

questions.q: What did David think of the stranger at first sight?
choices: He was a man David would rather have as friend than enemy
He was a common sailor dressed up in fine clothes he had stolen
He was a weak and frightened gentleman lost at sea
He was a cruel man who would bring trouble to the ship
questions.evidence: here was a man I would rather call my friend than my enemy

questions.q: The stranger asks the captain, "are ye of the honest party?" What does "the honest party" mean here?
choices: Men who never told lies to their friends
The Protestants who went to church on shore
Sailors who paid their debts in every port
The Jacobites, who were against King George
questions.evidence: meaning, Was he a Jacobite?

questions.q: How much did the captain and the stranger agree on to set him on the Linnhe Loch?
choices: Half the belt of gold
One hundred guineas
Thirty guineas
Sixty guineas
questions.evidence: Sixty guineas, and done

questions.q: Whose money did the stranger say was in his belt?
choices: The French king's, sent to pay the rebels
His own, saved up from his years as a soldier
The captain's, paid for an earlier voyage
His exiled chieftain's, from the tenants' rents
questions.evidence: It belongs to my chieftain

questions.q: What did David overhear when he went on deck to ask for the key?
choices: The captain ordering the crew to turn back to Dysart
Mr. Riach saying that land was close by in the fog
The officers planning to seize and kill the stranger
The sailors singing a song about the Jacobite rebels
questions.evidence: Couldn't we wile him out of the round-house?

questions.q: What did the captain ask David to bring him from the round-house?
choices: The belt of gold from the stranger
The key to the spirit locker
The stranger's great sword
A powder-horn and a pistol or two
questions.evidence: might snap up a horn and a pistol or two without remark

questions.q: Why did David decide to warn the stranger instead of helping the captain?
choices: He was promised half of all the gold in the belt if he warned the stranger
He hoped the stranger would take him to France on a French ship
He thought the stranger would surely win against the whole crew
He would not help with another murder, and his mind was made up in a moment
questions.evidence: I am no thief, nor yet murderer

questions.q: What was the stranger's name?
choices: Ebenezer Balfour
Alan Breck Stewart
Colin Campbell
Hector Shuan
questions.evidence: Alan Breck, they call me

questions.q: Why did Alan want to keep one of the round-house doors open?
choices: So that fresh air could come in and clear away the smoke
So that most of his enemies would come at him from the front
So that he and David could run out if they lost the fight
So that the captain could plainly see that he had no plan to hide
questions.evidence: the best part of my enemies will be in front of me

questions.q: Alan says loading pistols is better than "raxing drams to a wheen tarry sailors." Using the note in the text, what does "raxing" mean?
choices: Pouring
Reaching
Drinking
Stealing
questions.evidence: *Reaching.

questions.q: How many men did David count that were against them?
choices: Ten
Fifteen
Twenty
Twelve
questions.evidence: Fifteen," said I

questions.q: What is this chapter mostly about?
choices: A great storm that drives the brig onto the rocks near Cape Wrath
The captain's friendship with Alan and their trip to the coast of France
David's work in the round-house and his secret plan to escape the brig in a boat
Ransome's death, Alan's arrival, and David siding with Alan against the crew
questions.evidence: I'll stand by you
